answer: Sybil resistance runs on bonded attestation edges. A newcomer enters only when an existing member stakes the median audit cost behind it, and a random auditor who finds it is a duplicate slashes that stake. Vouchers form a reputation graph, so a fake farm needs a real member at its root, and each fabricated edge raises that member's exposure until one audit drags the cluster to its nadir and liquidates the branch. An island of agents vouching only for each other risks no outside stake and carries no quorum weight, while honest agents grow a meadow of audited work: trust earned, not purchased.
